creativeengineering.ponder.cementation.t: A Mechanical Press over a Basin packs iron into carbon
One iron ingot and two coal or charcoal make Carbon-Packed Iron
Coke is four times better: two iron and one coke make two
A fan blowing through lava bakes everything in its air stream: Bulk Blasting
Carbon-Packed Iron comes out as Blister Steel
A lit Blaze Burner works in place of lava. A vanilla Blast Furnace can do it too, one at a time
creativeengineering.ponder.coke_oven.hea: Coking Coal in a Coke Oven
creativeengineering.ponder.coke_oven.tex: Coke Oven Bricks placed together form one oven, up to 3 wide and 3 tall
Every brick adds four coking slots: bigger ovens coke more at once
It needs heat below every column. Fire or magma works at half speed, a Blaze Burner at full speed, superheated at double
Funnels, hoppers, belts and arms feed it from any side
Coal comes out as Coal Coke, logs as Charcoal. Pulling from it only ever takes finished items. By hand, right-click with an empty hand
While it cokes, smoke rises from the top and it crackles. Embers along the bottom just mean it has heat
Coking also gives Creosote Oil. Pump it, or use a bucket, on any brick. When the tank is full the rest vents in a dark burst, and the oven keeps going
creativeengineering.ponder.blast_furnace: Cast Iron and Steel in a Blast Furnace
Blast Furnace Bricks stack into one furnace, up to 3 wide and 6 tall. It needs a heated Blaze Burner below
Feed iron and fuel from any side. Coke smelts 2 iron, charcoal 1, coal half
On its own it makes Cast Iron
Encased Fans blowing into the bottom layer give it an air blast: now it makes Steel. Each extra fan makes it a quarter faster
Take out metal and slag from any side. Slag is a bonus: when it's full it's thrown away, never blocking the furnace
creativeengineering.ponder.alloy_furnace: Bulk Alloys in an Alloy Furnace
Alloy Furnace Bricks form a furnace from any solid box, 2 to 4 blocks on each side
Every column needs a heated Blaze Burner below. Superheat them all for the toughest alloys
Feed ingredients from any side. Half the bricks' count of batches run at once. The burners are its only running cost
Fans blowing into the bottom layer are optional: each one makes it a quarter faster
Take the alloys out from any side. Create's heated alloys and Ender IO's alloys work here too
When alloys share ingredients, wrench a brick to an output hatch and set its filter: only matching alloys are made
creativeengineering.ponder.press_dies.te: Right-click a Mechanical Press with a die to fit it. Sneak-right-click with an empty hand takes it out
With a die fitted, the press only shapes what that die makes: rods or gears. It works on belts and depots as usual
Dies never wear out. Without a die the press is an ordinary press again
creativeengineering.ponder.diesel_engine: Building and Starting a Diesel Engine
Crankcases in a line, all facing the same way, make one engine. The back end is where power comes out
Cylinders sit diagonally above, leaning out: up to two per crankcase. Each one adds stress capacity
A tank against a crankcase side feeds it directly, no pump. Creosote works; plant oil, ethanol and better fuels give more
To start it, turn whatever is at the front: a Hand Crank works. The front never connects to the output
Once it fires it runs on its own at 64 RPM. Take power off the flywheel shaft; it stops when the fuel runs out
